steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Conduction: heat transfer through direct contact — e.g. pan on hob transferring heat to food through the metal. Best for: frying, sautéing, griddling.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Convection: heat transfer through fluid (liquid or air) movement — hot fluid rises, cool fluid sinks, creating currents. Best for: baking (hot air), boiling/simmering (hot water), roasting.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Radiation: heat transfer through electromagnetic waves without needing a medium — e.g. grilling, toasting. The heat source emits infrared radiation that is absorbed by the food surface.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Microwave cooking: microwaves (electromagnetic waves) cause water molecules in food to vibrate rapidly, generating heat through friction. Microwaves penetrate about 4cm, so thick foods cook from outside in. Not suitable for pastry or crispy textures.
